provinces.name: Drenthe
provinces.description: Forests, heathlands and peaceful villages in the northeast of the country.
provinces.history: Dolmens, known as hunebedden, recall the prehistoric inhabitants of the region. Farming and peatland reclamation shaped its landscape.

provinces.name: Flevoland
provinces.description: Open spaces, polders and cities on land reclaimed from the water.
provinces.history: The area was created by draining parts of the former Zuiderzee inlet. Flevoland became the twelfth province in 1986.

provinces.name: Friesland
provinces.description: Lakes, canals, the northern coast and a distinctive Frisian culture.
provinces.history: The region is linked to the history of the Frisians. Maritime trade, farming and flood protection shaped its towns and villages.

provinces.name: Gelderland
provinces.description: The forests of the Veluwe, river valleys and historic cities in the east.
provinces.history: The province takes its name from historic Guelders. The Duchy of Guelders played a significant role in the medieval Netherlands.

provinces.name: Groningen
provinces.description: Northern polders and a lively university city at the heart of the province.
provinces.history: The region developed around the city of Groningen and the surrounding Ommelanden. Trade and agriculture connected the city to the coast.

provinces.name: Limburg
provinces.description: A southern province along the Meuse, with hills and border towns.
provinces.history: Roman heritage, medieval territories and the proximity of Belgium and Germany left their mark on the region's culture and architecture.

provinces.name: North Brabant
provinces.description: Historic cities, museums, design and green spaces in the south.
provinces.history: The province is linked to the historic Duchy of Brabant. Industrial development later transformed cities such as Eindhoven and Tilburg.

provinces.name: North Holland
provinces.description: Amsterdam's canals, North Sea dunes and old trading towns.
provinces.history: Maritime trade had a major influence on the region. The modern province emerged when Holland was divided into northern and southern parts.

provinces.name: Overijssel
provinces.description: Hanseatic cities, rivers, rural landscapes and waterways.
provinces.history: Zwolle, Kampen and Deventer grew through Hanseatic trading connections. Industry shaped the development of Twente in the east of the province.

provinces.name: Utrecht
provinces.description: A central province with canals, country estates and wooded hills.
provinces.history: The city of Utrecht grew beside a Roman fort and became an important religious center. Its influence can be seen throughout the province's history.

provinces.name: Zeeland
provinces.description: Open seascapes, island landscapes, dikes and port towns.
provinces.history: Life in Zeeland was shaped by maritime trade and the struggle against the sea. After the flood of 1953, coastal protection became part of the Delta Works.

provinces.name: South Holland
provinces.description: Rotterdam, The Hague, historic towns and a dense network of waterways.
provinces.history: The region developed through trade, ports and national government. The modern province was formed when Holland was divided.

cities.name: Assen
cities.description: The small capital of Drenthe, with a museum, parks and a peaceful center.
cities.history: The town developed around a medieval monastery and later became the administrative center of Drenthe.

cities.name: Lelystad
cities.description: A city on a polder where the history of land reclamation comes to life.
cities.history: Lelystad was built on reclaimed land and named after Cornelis Lely.

cities.name: Leeuwarden
cities.description: The capital of Friesland, with canals, museums and welcoming squares.
cities.history: This old trading town became the administrative and cultural center of Friesland.

cities.name: Arnhem
cities.description: A green city beside the Rhine, close to the natural landscapes of the Veluwe.
cities.history: Arnhem is known for its trading past and the Battle of Arnhem during the Second World War.

cities.name: Groningen
cities.description: A university city with lively streets and distinctive architecture.
cities.history: Groningen was a regional trading center. Its university became an important part of city life.

cities.name: Maastricht
cities.description: A city on the Meuse with stone streets, squares and historic churches.
cities.history: A Roman river crossing and medieval trade played important roles in Maastricht's development.

cities.name: ’s-Hertogenbosch
cities.description: A city of canals and medieval streets, also known as Den Bosch.
cities.history: The city developed as a fortified town in the Duchy of Brabant.

cities.name: Haarlem
cities.description: A historic city near the dunes and the North Sea coast.
cities.history: Brewing, textiles and art played important roles in the city's history.

cities.name: Zwolle
cities.description: A city with a historic center, fortifications and museums.
cities.history: Zwolle belonged to the Hanseatic League, which connected trading cities across northern Europe.

cities.name: Utrecht
cities.description: Canals with waterside wharves and a medieval center.
cities.history: A Roman fort preceded the development of the city. In the Middle Ages, Utrecht became an influential religious center.

cities.name: Middelburg
cities.description: The capital of Zeeland, with canals, historic facades and an abbey.
cities.history: Maritime trade helped the city grow. Middelburg was a significant trading center in the Netherlands.

cities.name: The Hague
cities.description: A city of museums, government buildings and seaside scenery.
cities.history: The Hague grew beside the residence of the Counts of Holland and became the center of national government.

cities.name: Amsterdam
cities.description: Canals, museums and neighborhoods of narrow waterside facades.
cities.history: The city grew around a dam on the Amstel River. Maritime trade had a particularly strong influence on its development in the seventeenth century.

cities.name: Rotterdam
cities.description: A port city with modern architecture and waterfronts along the Meuse.
cities.history: The growth of the port turned Rotterdam into a major trading center. Much of the city was rebuilt after the destruction of the Second World War.

cities.name: Emmen
cities.description: A town in eastern Drenthe, close to natural landscapes and ancient monuments.
cities.history: Peatland reclamation and industrial development contributed to Emmen's growth.

cities.name: Eindhoven
cities.description: A city of technology, design and reinvented industrial spaces.
cities.history: The growth of Philips played an important role in turning Eindhoven into an industrial and technological center.

cities.name: Meppel
cities.description: A canal town in southwestern Drenthe, with small squares and historic buildings.
cities.history: Waterways connected Meppel to the peatlands of Drenthe. Peat transport and trade helped the town grow.

cities.name: Coevorden
cities.description: A historic town in southern Drenthe with a castle, canals and traces of its fortress layout.
cities.history: Its strategic position made Coevorden an important fortress on the route to the northern territories. The castle and surviving fortifications recall its military past.

cities.name: Almere
cities.description: A modern city with unusual architecture, parks and expanses of water.
cities.history: Almere was founded on reclaimed land in Southern Flevoland. Its history is linked to the creation of new towns and planning life on the polders.

cities.name: Zeewolde
cities.description: A young town on Lake Veluwemeer, near forests, beaches and land art.
cities.history: Zeewolde emerged during the settlement of reclaimed Southern Flevoland. Its development is linked to agriculture, new housing and waterside recreation.

cities.name: Sneek
cities.description: A Frisian town of canals and water sports, ideal for exploring the lake district.
cities.history: Sneek developed as a trading town in the Middle Ages. Shipbuilding and water sports later became prominent parts of local life.

cities.name: Harlingen
cities.description: A port town on the Wadden Sea, with historic warehouses, harbors and canals.
cities.history: Trade and shipping shaped Harlingen's character. Its old houses and harbor structures preserve memories of the town's maritime past.

cities.name: Nijmegen
cities.description: A city above the River Waal with a historic center and waterfronts.
cities.history: Nijmegen is linked to the Roman history of the Netherlands. Fortifications, trade and river routes shaped the city over the following centuries.

cities.name: Apeldoorn
cities.description: A green city beside the forests of the Veluwe, known for its palace and spacious parks.
cities.history: Apeldoorn's history is closely linked to Het Loo Palace, a former residence of the Dutch royal family. The palace and gardens became important parts of the city's cultural heritage.

cities.name: Appingedam
cities.description: A small historic town on the Damsterdiep canal, known for its houses over the water.
cities.history: The old center retains medieval features. Its position on the Damsterdiep connected the town's life to waterways and trade.

cities.name: Delfzijl
cities.description: A port town on the Ems estuary, with a waterfront and a maritime character.
cities.history: Delfzijl's development is linked to its locks, port and shipping. Its maritime and regional heritage is represented in local museum collections.

cities.name: Venlo
cities.description: A city on the Meuse near the German border, with squares and museums.
cities.history: River routes and its border location encouraged trade. Venlo's history is part of Limburg's story, from early settlements to the modern city.

cities.name: Roermond
cities.description: A historic city beside the Meuse and Roer, near the Maasplassen lakes.
cities.history: Roermond's past survives in its old streets, churches and monuments. Local history exhibitions explore the city's development and the lives of its residents.

cities.name: Breda
cities.description: A city of historic squares, green parks and Nassau family heritage.
cities.history: Breda was an important center of the Nassau estates. Their influence survives in the castle, old center and the city's great church.

cities.name: Tilburg
cities.description: A city of textile heritage, contemporary design and reinvented factory districts.
cities.history: Wool production made Tilburg an industrial center of Brabant. Today, textile history sits alongside art and modern technology.

cities.name: Alkmaar
cities.description: A city of canals and historic squares, known for its cheese-trading traditions.
cities.history: Trade in agricultural produce and cheese became part of the city's identity. The old center and weighing-house square recall Alkmaar's trading past.

cities.name: Hoorn
cities.description: A historic port town with harbors and old facades.
cities.history: Hoorn is linked to maritime trade and long-distance voyages. Its history encompasses both the growth of a port town and the colonial past of Dutch trade.

cities.name: Deventer
cities.description: A Hanseatic city on the IJssel, with historic streets and the Brink square.
cities.history: Trade along the IJssel and Hanseatic connections helped Deventer develop. Its medieval past remains visible in the center.

cities.name: Enschede
cities.description: A city in Twente where industrial heritage meets culture and education.
cities.history: The textile industry had a major influence on Enschede. Former industrial spaces are now used for cultural projects, among other activities.

cities.name: Amersfoort
cities.description: A city of canals, old streets and surviving fortified gates.
cities.history: Medieval fortifications shaped Amersfoort. The Koppelpoort recalls a time when both roads and waterways needed protection.

cities.name: Wijk bij Duurstede
cities.description: A small historic town beside the Lek and Kromme Rijn rivers, with a castle and an old center.
cities.history: The town's medieval heritage is linked to Duurstede Castle and the history of the river region. The castle, churches and old streets preserve traces of this past.

cities.name: Vlissingen
cities.description: A maritime city on the Western Scheldt, with a long promenade and views of passing ships.
cities.history: The port, trade and shipbuilding shaped Vlissingen's history. Its maritime heritage survives in historic buildings and museum collections.

cities.name: Goes
cities.description: A town in South Beveland with a historic center and an old harbor.
cities.history: The history of Goes is linked to trade and life in Beveland. Flooding and land reclamation changed the surrounding landscape and influenced the region's development.

cities.name: Delft
cities.description: A city of canals, pottery and picturesque squares between The Hague and Rotterdam.
cities.history: Delft is known for its blue-and-white pottery and its connection to the painter Johannes Vermeer. Art and craftsmanship remain important parts of its identity.

cities.name: Leiden
cities.description: A city of canals, university traditions and museums.
cities.history: Textile production, science and art play important roles in Leiden's history. Museum collections reveal how life in the city changed over time.

attractions.name: Drents Museum

attractions.name: Batavialand
attractions.description: A museum about water, shipbuilding and the history of polder reclamation.

attractions.name: Fries Museum
attractions.description: A museum of the art, culture and history of Friesland.

attractions.name: Netherlands Open Air Museum
attractions.description: Historic buildings and stories of everyday life in the Netherlands.

attractions.name: Groninger Museum
attractions.description: An art museum in a distinctive waterside building.

attractions.name: Bonnefanten
attractions.description: An art museum on the banks of the Meuse.

attractions.name: North Brabant Museum
attractions.description: The art and history of the province of North Brabant.

attractions.name: Frans Hals Museum
attractions.description: Painting and the artistic heritage of Haarlem.

attractions.name: Museum de Fundatie
attractions.description: A fine art collection and temporary exhibitions.

attractions.name: Dom Tower
attractions.description: A medieval tower and one of Utrecht's main landmarks.

attractions.name: Zeeuws Museum
attractions.description: The history and culture of Zeeland in a medieval abbey building.

attractions.name: Mauritshuis
attractions.description: An art museum known for its collection of paintings by Dutch masters.

attractions.name: Rijksmuseum
attractions.description: The national museum of art and history of the Netherlands.

attractions.name: Cube Houses
attractions.description: An unusual housing complex, with a museum house that reveals its interior design.

attractions.name: WILDLANDS
attractions.description: A zoo with several themed natural environments.

attractions.name: Philips Museum
attractions.description: The history of Philips and its connection to the city.

attractions.name: Museum Indruk
attractions.description: A museum of printing and graphic craftsmanship, from typesetting to printing presses.

attractions.name: Coevorden Municipal Museum
attractions.description: Exhibitions about the history of the town and its residents in the historic Arsenal building.

attractions.name: The Green Cathedral
attractions.description: A work of land art by Marinus Boezem, in which trees trace the outline of a Gothic cathedral.

attractions.name: Sea Level
attractions.description: Richard Serra's work in De Wetering park helps visitors visualize the relationship between sea level and reclaimed land.

attractions.name: Frisian Maritime Museum
attractions.description: The history of Frisian shipping, winter sports and Sneek itself.

attractions.name: Hannemahuis
attractions.description: A museum of Harlingen's culture and history in a historic town house.

attractions.name: Valkhof Museum
attractions.description: A museum of archaeology and art, including the region's Roman heritage. Check the website for current visiting arrangements before you go.

attractions.name: Het Loo Palace
attractions.description: Palace interiors, gardens and exhibitions about the House of Orange.

attractions.name: Hanging Kitchens
attractions.description: Extensions of old houses projecting over the Damsterdiep canal, a distinctive symbol of Appingedam.

attractions.name: MuzeeAquarium
attractions.description: Regional nature and history alongside an aquarium of marine life from the Wadden Sea and North Sea.

attractions.name: Limburgs Museum
attractions.description: Stories of Limburg's residents, archaeology and regional culture in interactive exhibitions.

attractions.name: Roermond History House
attractions.description: An exhibition about the city's development and past in the public library building.

attractions.name: Great Church of Breda
attractions.description: A Gothic church with monuments and tombs of the Nassau family.

attractions.name: TextielMuseum
attractions.description: A museum of textiles, art and design with a working experimental studio, TextielLab.

attractions.name: Dutch Cheese Museum
attractions.description: The history of cheesemaking and the journey from milk to finished cheese.

attractions.name: The Story of Hoorn — Statenpoort
attractions.native_name: Ontdek het verhaal van Hoorn — Statenpoort
attractions.description: A multimedia account of the city's history by the Westfries Museum in the Statenpoort building.

attractions.name: Museum De Waag
attractions.description: The city's history and Deventer collections in the historic weighing-house building.

attractions.name: De Museumfabriek
attractions.description: A family museum combining the history of Twente, science and hands-on discovery.

attractions.name: Koppelpoort
attractions.description: Historic gates combining a land passage and a water passage.

attractions.name: Duurstede Castle
attractions.description: A medieval castle with towers and a surrounding park. Access depends on events taking place; check visiting arrangements on the website.

attractions.name: Zeeland Maritime Museum
attractions.description: A museum about the sea, shipping and the people connected to Zeeland's maritime history.

attractions.name: De Bevelanden Historical Museum
attractions.description: The history of Goes and Beveland, local collections and stories of life among water and polders.

attractions.name: Royal Delft Museum
attractions.description: A historic collection of Delft pottery and an introduction to traditional Delft Blue production.

attractions.name: Museum De Lakenhal
attractions.description: The art and history of Leiden in its former cloth hall.
